utterances.text: That's right. There was no intention on their part of doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, how that paramilitary demonstrated their intentions, and how did that army let it be known that they did not wish to be deactivated? How did they manifest that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that army or, rather, those forces that had collected together in Dubrovnik had already been in armed combat beforehand, from the 1st of October up until the 25th of October, in the fighting around town. The members the paramilitary formations of Croatia or, rather, the MUP and the ZNG, they launched combat operations, engaged in combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that when the term "town" or when there's a question about Dubrovnik that there be specificity. There is Dubrovnik municipality, there is municipal city Dubrovnik, and then there is the core, the Old Town, and the record is far from clear what is being referred to in counsel's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I say I've understood all of this to be referring to the broader area of Dubrovnik municipality, not dealing with the Old Town, because as I understood it, when Mr. Rodic intends to refer to the Old Town, he will do so specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have not asked any questions related to the Old Town as yet, but I will, of course, emphasise that when I do come to ask questions of that type. And we've already clarified the fact that the Dubrovnik municipality covers an area from the borders -- or, rather, the witness can help us there. Let's repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, could you tell us, roughly speaking, the area incorporated by the Dubrovnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's an area from the border of the Republic of Croatia and its borders with Montenegro. So we have Prevlaka, Debeli Brijeg on the one side, and Ston, the Dubrovnik littoral, and Ston as the last point on that side. It stretches for an area of approximately 100 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And when you say the town of Dubrovnik, can you tell us what area you're referring to, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am thinking of the urban area of town, from the Belvedere Hotel on the south right down to the Sustjepan peninsula in the Dubrovnik Rijeka and in-depth -- that is the urban area of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is that urban area several kilometres long?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly its length?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, width-wise between the Belvedere and the Sustjepan peninsula it might be about four to five kilometres, that axis, the horizontal axis. And the vertical axis from the Petak peninsula to Komolac is about six kilometres, five to six.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Although we haven't mentioned this but we'll come to that in due course, but since we're explaining all this, when you say "Stari Grad," "Old Town," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I say "Stari Grad," "Old Town," it is an enclave within Dubrovnik proper, and it is surrounded by a wall, ramparts that are three to four metres high with turrets or towers at each corner of this quadrangle, the dimensions being approximately 700 metres horizontally and one kilometre vertically, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true and correct that your units, on the 15th of October, entered Cavtat without any combat? And I'm talking about the 15th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This entry into Cavtat, was it made possible through negotiations and communication with the inhabitants of Cavtat themselves?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we appealed to the citizens. We told them that the non-combat units would enter town, but I'm not quite sure how it actually took place. All I do know is this: That there was no fighting. We did not open fire on the town from any weapons or artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me why, then, you took control of Kupari, why you landed and took control of Kupari and not the way you did -- and you didn't in Cavtat?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we bore in mind the fact that Kupari was a military recreational centre which was -- had been usurped. It had been taken over by Croatian forces, and they defended it with guns, with cannons that inflicted harm on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which Croatian forces you mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were forces we mentioned a moment ago, the ZNG forces specifically, and over there were parts of a company and a whole command of a lower order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: These Croatian forces in Kupari, did they have heavy weapons at all?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They had two cannons, one that we seized, one 85-millimetre cannon, and another one which was 76-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was this -- these -- were these artillery pieces used by the Croatian forces from Kupari to target JNA forces?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any casualties on the side of the JNA through this targeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did have casualties in the battles before the landing operation itself, several casualties. Several men were wounded, and I think two were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you consider the attack on Kupari to be a legitimate military operation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, and I was given the assignment of taking control of Kupari.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, after having taken control of Kupari, why did you take control of the Dubac-Zarkovica-Brgat line afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given the assignment to proceed and take the line, the ridge, and to gain control of the communications and roads from Dubrovnik to Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know what you wrote in your combat report and proposed to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group immediately after the 24th of October when you took control of Kupari? Do you know why you proposed what you proposed?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean what I asked you a moment ago, the proposal to reach the Dubac-Zarkovica-Brgat line, because that was after Kupari, right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In taking control of Zupa after Kupari, I think that we suffered the heaviest losses from the artillery in the Dubac region, Belvedere, and a stone quarry above a small church called St. Anne's church. And there was strong artillery fire coming from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does that then mean that by taking control of Kupari you were not able to complete your combat operation around Dubrovnik for the reasons you've just given us?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We were not able to persevere there because it was a hole. Zupa with its settlements and Kupari are found in a depression dominated by elevations at the ridge along the line Gornji Brgat-Dubac-Zarkovica, that axis, and the quarry that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it true then that you had to take control there because of the enemy activities -- enemy activities at the accesses to Dubrovnik, that that's why you had to undertake that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me why you were forced from the Dubac-Zarkovica-Brgat line or access to come closer to Dubrovnik or, rather, to take control of the fortress at Bosanka Strincijera?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 26th of October, there was a cease-fire which came into force, and that cease-fire lasted until the 8th of November. There was no combat, no fighting during that truce. Otherwise, if I might be allowed to add, the entire Dubrovnik operation, as far as active combat is concerned and active operations, was ten days active operations and all the rest was a cease-fire or, rather, inactivity. Ten active days, and the rest was non-active.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, the Croatian forces from Bosanka and Strincijera, did they open fire at the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know what weapons they had there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Bosanka was taken, as far as I can remember, two recoilless guns were captured, two racket launchers of the Fagot type, and one 20-millimetre gun. And I don't know. I think one or two machine-guns, heavy machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were any mortars captured?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think two 82-millimetre mortars, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any hand-held launchers that were taken?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hand-held launchers? That is light weaponry, so it is not included in artillery. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember that before that, from Bosanka and Strincijera, the Croat forces attacked the JNA and caused losses among them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Could we get a time frame on this, please, a time frame for the action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. It's not very clear, is it, Mr. Rodic. Is it before the 26th of October or later?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the 26th of October, Your Honour. Through these questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Between the 26th of October and the 8th of November, that is to say before the attack on Bosanka, that period is considered to be one of a cease-fire, that is to say when a cease-fire was in force. However, there were -- there was such a lot of provocative action taken on both sides that there were losses on our side and on their side. On these fortresses that have just been referred to, Bosanka, Strincijera, Gradci and Srdj, which constituted the key to the defence of this ridge, there were choice forces of the defence of Dubrovnik. They were heavy fortified in the fortresses, and therefore, they were in a position to successfully defend all approaches to town. Due to these provocations, often there were losses, and even strong artillery fire was used from both sides. The Defence of Dubrovnik believed that there would be an attack launched against town, bearing in mind the fact that there were strong forces around the town, our forces, four to five battalions in total. These forces reacted rather nervously by firing projectiles at our parts, and our forces, in turn, responded with the same kind of fire or even stronger fire. Then on the 8th of November, the order came from the 2nd Operational Group command to take Bosanka, because the defenders of Bosanka hindered communication between Brgat and Zarkovica, the only communication there was for bringing supplies to Zarkovica. That was the only communication route. Then our action continued when Bosanka was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I have to interrupt you, because your answer is an expanded one, and my question was the following: Before Bosanka was taken and before Strincijera was taken by the JNA, did the JNA suffer any losses due to the action taken by Croat forces from those positions? And I still have not received an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I've said that already, that there were losses due to these provocations. There were losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were any members of the JNA killed?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the attack on Bosanka, there were perhaps two dead and a few wounded, but the greatest losses were sustained after the attack on Bosanka, between the 8th and the 10th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That perhaps is a convenient time, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I ask the usher's assistance, please. Could we have a document distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Jokic, whether you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that through this document you are proposing to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group that you receive within the 9th VPS a motorised battalion to be resubordinated to you from Bar?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: As the document is addressed to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group and the commander of the 2nd Corps, to his attention as well, does that mean that the -- no. I apologise. That the motorised battalion from Bar, is it within the composition of the 2nd Corps? Was it under them first and you are requesting that it be placed under your command, or is there something else, is this something else?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I haven't seen this document. I'm not quite clear, because this was never actually realised. The 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade, at that time it was on leave, but it returned several days later. So this was never put into practice, it was never executed. So I don't remember this document at all in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But do you remember whether operations were planned in the region of the village of Orasec, Brsine and Gromaca?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was outside my area. Had nothing to do with me. At the time, on the 30th of October, we had not assumed control of Dubrovacka Rijeka or Komolac or Mokosica at all, and in my units were not there at all, so it's got nothing to do with this. And the 133rd Motorised Brigade that's mentioned here is a brigade from Bar which did not take part in the operation. So I don't really know what this is about. This document is one I do not recognise at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you have units in the Uskoplje region at all?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Uskoplje is in the area of responsibility of the brigade -- of the 482nd Brigade, which was not subordinated to me or, rather, it was subordinated but on the 30th of October, we had no operations outside this zone. I mean, Gromaca is in the area of the 2nd Corps, in their zone. Orasec as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the villages mentioned here, Gromaca, Orasec, and Brsine, that that was in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps? Is that is it? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So the beginning of the sentence refers to that, does it, and that is why this document is being sent to the 2nd Corps for their information when it says for planned activities in the region, bearing in mind that you returned the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade? You are then informing the command of the 2nd Op Group and the 2nd Corps and that that is why you are suggesting that the motorised brigade from Bar be attached to you, be resubordinated to you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that the document is quite illogical. There's no logical to it. And it was never implemented. My units were not operational and active, and this never came into being. The battalion never came under me within the composition of my unit. This brigade, I think, was from Pula which disembarked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, I don't suppose you challenge that this is a document from the command of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can see that judging by what it says at the top, but I don't think it is a logical document, and none of what it says here was ever put into practice. It was absolutely impossible for my unit to be operational in the region of Brsine, Orasec, and Gromaca, which is 30 or 40 kilometres away from my first units, so it was the zone of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. But just tell me if this document is authentic. Would you say it's authentic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would appear to be authentic, but as I say, none of this was of implemented and it does not reflect the state of affairs, the actual state of affairs, how things stood.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may we have a number, a Defence number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me. The witness has not accepted that the document actually represents something that his own units were responsible for, and we would object to its admission in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I agree with what you've put, but he does accept on its face the document itself as something emanating from his command, although he can't understand it. So it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be marked D48.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please distribute the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell me whether this document is familiar to you, and is it an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this document. It is an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The document is from the command of the 9th VPS. It is dated the 6th of November, 1991. Tell me, please, is that the time that you mentioned before the break, between the 26th of October and the 8th of November when there was supposed to be a cease-fire in force?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Since the 472nd Motorised Brigade at this period was within the composition of the 9th VPS Military Naval Sector, through this order are you prohibiting any opening fire by the artillery with the aim of creating conditions for negotiations between the representatives of the 2nd Operational Group and the European mission in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In this order, you say that the artillery can be used only from orders from the command post and forward command post of the 9th VPS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a reason why this was written. Before this event -- if I might be allowed to explain, Your Honour. Before this particular event --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were provocations, and that led to the writing of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. But what I'm interested in is this: I'm interested in the last sentence, where it says: "This order does not exclude the obligations of the units and command of the 472nd Motorised Brigade to suggest the use of artillery if they evaluate it as necessary." Could you explain that sentence to us, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the use of the artillery is forbidden and if the unit is threatened because of the activity of the other side, then the unit can come into action, it can react or, rather, propose that a reaction follow but not to resort to the use of arms. So a proposal isn't the same thing as an order to use weapons. So the superior officer will decide whether he is going to accept the proposal or not. That's the sense of this, the gist of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I have understood the explanation you have just given, but within the context of all this, your order does not exclude the obligation on the part of the units and the command of this brigade to propose the use of weapons should they deem necessary. That means that they are duty-bound to propose the deployment of the artillery if they think the situation merits that. So can you explain to us what kind of situation that would be to merit its use?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if I've been clear enough. If they feel that they are threatened, that their positions are threatened, that the positions of the unit are threatened that they are supporting or that their own positions have come under threat, then they can propose to the superior command that they be deployed. They can propose that they go into action.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What you say, they can propose, is that the gist of it or do they have the obligation to propose if they are threatened and if they assess that this is necessary, as it says here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Each unit is duty-bound if it comes under threat and if it deems necessary that it should react, has the obligation to propose to its superior commander the way in which they are to open fire. That's a general principle in every operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may we have a number for this document, marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before that, perhaps you could tell me, Admiral, to whom would the command of the 472nd Brigade suggest the use of artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to the superior command. The superior command would be the 9th Sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is your own command.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, my own command, with the proviso that this unit, on this particular date, was to have left subordination to my command and left the zone pursuant to orders by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group. So that is the only point that can be contested, the fact that the order was never carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. This document will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D49.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In respect of this period, the beginning of the month of November, 1991, you mentioned that there were provocations then in that part of the territory, around Dubrovnik, that is. Can you tell me, in relation to these provocations, did you write any reports to anyone? Did you brief anyone about this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of November, there were two reports regarding provocations in the area where the approaches to the town of Dubrovnik were and also neighbourhoods outside the Old Town. One report, I think, is from the 1st or 2nd of November and was written by the command of the 2nd Operational Group. The second one was addressed to me. I think I wrote it on the 3rd or 4th of November. I wrote it to Admiral Brovet, and it had to do with provocations related to the 472nd Brigade or its battalions or, rather, its battalions facing the town of Dubrovnik and the neighbourhoods on the approaches to town.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Rodic's microphone please be turned on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to have the following document distributed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If you're reading the handwritten part, I'll help you. It says: "Colonel S. Lukic, Lieutenant Colonel Svicevic, familiarise the general; and act on his decision." Do you know whose signature this is underneath the handwritten text? The handwritten text.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it perhaps Colonel Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does the Deputy Federal Secretary, Admiral Brovet, through this document, ask urgently for information regarding the allegations from the protest of the International Monitoring Mission of the European Community from the 3rd of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it stated that this document should be sent, number one, to the commander of the 9th VPS - to you - and secondly, to the commander of the 2nd OG?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document please be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could help me, Admiral. It's not clear from these documents. Are you talking of provocations to units under your command, in particular the 472nd Brigade, or are you speaking of provocations by them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this pertains to the request of the representatives of the European Community addressed to General Brovet to establish responsibility for provocations of the units of the 472nd Brigade vis-a-vis the defenders of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In this document that Brovet is sending you and the commander of the 2nd OG, is there a single reference to the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no reference there, but there is in the response.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, but did you receive the text of the protest of the Monitoring Mission of the European Community addressed to the Federal Secretary?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did receive it. I don't know why that protest is not there in addition to that document which is just an accompanying letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you received it or not or are you just making this assumption?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to have received it. Since I gave a reply, I had to have received it. And I see from the text that this group of officers are the ones who were engaged in negotiations, and they were entrusted by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group to carry out these negotiations, and this probably went through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you act in accordance with this request put forth by Admiral Brovet?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And who was it that you informed about this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who asked for this, that is to say the -- Admiral Brovet and the command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to give the witness document P104. That is a Prosecution exhibit. It is under tab 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said that you had not seen this document before when my learned friend of the Prosecution asked you about it during the examination-in-chief, but you also said that you were aware of the events referred to in this document; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This document, is it one that is sent by the command of the 2nd Operational Group to the operational centre, to Admiral Stane Brovet in person, precisely in response the request of Admiral Brovet's that we saw a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did General Strugar receive a report from you in relation to the allegations made by the Croatian side or, rather, the Monitoring Mission of the European Community? As regards paragraph 5. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I don't know whether it exists in the archives, but he must have received one. We must have provided him with an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And did you report to him about the chemical warfare agents referred to in the protest of the European Monitoring Mission?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you characterised such claims of the other side as deceit, and General Strugar, in his response, said that it was obvious that this was not true, that --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it true that when the 2nd Operational Group is sending such information to General -- to Admiral Brovet, does that mean that they believe your report?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did the Croatian forces use hotels in Dubrovnik as shelter for their own action?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They had artillery pieces and other equipment near hotels.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you have information to the effect that Croatian paramilitary forces were staying at hotels, that they were stationed there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were stationed in hotels, of course. It is a well-known thing, which hotels and which forces. And the commander of the defence of Dubrovnik did not deny that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In addition to the statement made by the commander of the Defence of the town of Dubrovnik, did you read any other statements while preparing your defence? Did you have statements made by other persons? Did you read intelligence reports? Did you have any made available to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please take a look at paragraph 2 where the 31st of October is referred to, that the monitors accused the JNA of wounding five civilians from a light machine-gun. They presented a list of names with a description of the injuries. However, a shrapnel that remained in a body is referred to there as well. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it from the text, but I don't know. I cannot recall this event, because I did not give any interpretations of that. I don't know. Or at least, I don't remember that it was my own men. I know that there were complaints referring to Lopud, that -- that mortars operated from there in relation to Petrovo Selo, et cetera. However, I cannot say whether it was maladjustment of the artillery pieces and that the shell exploded near Gruz and that is why it wounded these citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: However, the basic point of this complaint is that there were civilians injured by light machine-guns, and also reference is made to shrapnel, but it's not machine-guns that use any kind of ammunition that would result in shrapnel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph of paragraph -- in the second sentence of paragraph 2, it says: "It was reliably known that on that day the JNA did not in any way violate the cease-fire." Was this assertion based on a report obtained beforehand from the units involved as was the case with you under item 5 in reference to chemical warfare agents?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what the procedure would have to be in order to establish things in an objective manner and in order to give an answer that would be based on facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 4 and tell me whether on the basis of the reports of subordinates the response sent to Admiral Brovet was compiled on that basis? In paragraph 4, there is no denying that the JNA did open fire, but an explanation is provided as to when, where, and under what circumstances; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is hard for me to give an explanation because this information had been collected. It's probably the organs of the 2nd Operational Group that collected information in specific units, that is to say battalions of the brigade. And it is hard for me now -- well, I can give an explanation, but if that is what is written here, if that is objective and based on facts, then it absolutely sounds logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And how and in what way was it explained why the JNA opened fire on the 2nd of November?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can see from this that a caution was issued, a warning, that fire was opened at these units and their positions, and in order to prevent further threats to the lives of the soldiers, fire was met with fire. There was response. That's the sense of it. So the use of fire under the given circumstances is not challenged.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But is it mentioned that the JNA had sent a radiograph to the European -- EC Mission? A radiograph was sent that said, among other things, that they warned that their positions were being fired at.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would you take a look at paragraph 7 of this document now, please, and tell us what that is about.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this paragraph says that during talks on the 4th of November with representatives of the EC Mission, the JNA representative received a message at 1210 hours that fire was being opened at JNA positions from the old part of Dubrovnik town, and this was brought to the attention of the EC representatives. It was also pointed out that the Croatian side was trying, at all costs, to provoke the JNA in order to discredit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Judging by what it says in paragraph 7, does that mean that the JNA representative, in negotiations with the representatives of the EEC Mission received this piece of information and told them that by way of protest?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When it says that JNA positions were fired at from the old part of Dubrovnik town, does that mean the Old Town, the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's precisely what it means, the Old Town, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the EC representatives responded to this protest from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any response from the EC representatives once they had received protests from the JNA? Did they react in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that just on one occasion. I don't know exactly when, but I seem to remember that once they did take up a protest as a basis, but whether it was this particular protest or another protest that we lodged, I really can't remember which they acted upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, October to December 1991, was there just one justified protest from the JNA or more?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were probably several. I don't really know, but the fact is that the Croatian side or, rather, the Defence of Dubrovnik daily lodged protests. We did this very rarely, although I wasn't well-versed in all this, because if you wanted to lodge a protest, this was done by the team, the negotiating team, for the most part. And those negotiators were subordinated to the commander of the 2nd Operational Group, so that I know about some but probably not about most of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is one objection I wanted to raise without interrupting the Admiral. Line 11, "one justified protest," that is a value judgement put on by counsel and it's not defined. So I'd either ask to strike or have it explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's merely in a question. The answer of the witness is that he knows of only one protest that was ever acted on, but he says he doesn't know what other protests were made. So I think the matter's satisfactorily left at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In the area of your responsibility, the 9th Naval Military Sector, the 9th VPS, in the period from October to December 1991, did you have reason to protest to the other side or, rather, to the Crisis Staff of Dubrovnik or to the Monitoring Mission of the European Community? Did you have reason to lodge a protest? Was there reason for you to do that? Regardless of whether you did that or not, did you have reason to protest? And if so, why?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was reason. Of course there was, on several occasions. But as I've already said --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, these reasons for which you would lodge a protest --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The witness has not finished his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I felt he had. It was no doubt an innocent mistake. Yes. Were you wanting to say more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I wanted to finish by adding this: I said that there was just one protest, as far as I remember, that was accepted by the representatives of the European Community but that there were more protests. I don't know how many more, because these protests were lodged by negotiators at their meetings with the Crisis Staff. And that is why it is not for me to state how many protests were actually lodged and how many should have been lodged and weren't lodged. I think that the people in the command of the 2nd Operational Group would know about that better than me, as would the negotiating team of Colonel Svicevic. They would be better versed in these matters. And that's my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, I didn't ask you how many protests there were or what the dates were. And my question was a simple one: You were the commander of the 9th VPS. You had your area of responsibility and area for your units to operate in; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So as the commander of the 9th VPS, you yourself in the area of responsibility of your units, were there any soldiers killed, wounded during the proclaimed cease-fire or truce which was caused by the actions of the other side? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know something about that. And there were individual cases on the hand-over of duty of General Strugar, hand-over and take-over of duty of General Strugar. On that day there was a killing in an ambush by a sniper, by sniper fire, of my soldier. He was killed by sniper fire in the region around the village of Grude. And that took place on the 13th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was that a reason to lodge a protest? So I'm not asking you whether a protest was lodged or not; was that good reason to lodge a protest to the other side and to lodge it with the European representatives?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So I'm asking you once again, without asking you to enumerate the dates and specific instances and cases in the period of October, November, and December 1991, was there good reason, were there justifiable reasons because of the actions of the opposite side during a truce or cease-fire for the JNA to protest, lodge a protest with the Crisis Staff or with the EC Monitoring Mission?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course there was. There was reason for protests and because of the provocations that came from the other side, but all I said was that I don't know whether such protests were actually lodged. We didn't understand each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: From October to December 1991, did you have a number of killed and casualties, wounded, during the cease-fire or truce?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. There were several instances. I can list some of them for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, briefly, if you remember who they were.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to what I've already stated, the other example was -- took place in Cavtat around the Mlini area where a soldier called Barac was killed, and that was during a cease-fire or truce. I think it was on the 16th or 17th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there examples such as that after that date as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Greben or the ridge area where the firing came from Mount Srdj and Strincijera, in the firing from those points and provocations from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Whose provocations? Provocations by whom?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to assess. You don't always know who started first, who opened fire first.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: As the commander of the VPS at the time, were you informed that a fighters of yours, a soldier of yours had been killed or wounded as a result of the fire that was opened by the other side as provocation during the cease-fire or truce?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two cases in point, they are clear-cut cases, and I have stated them. As to the situation at Greben or the ridge, it was always very fluid because the fortresses up there were manned by extremists who opened fire with reason or without reason, with cause or without cause. And there were, of course, provocations on our part, too, because the distance between the towers and positions were so small that it was difficult to establish who actually opened fire first. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, Your Honour, but I thought we were working until 7.00 this evening. But if this is the right time, fine, no problem with that. We haven't had afternoon sittings for a long time, so I'm not sure whether the working -- the hours of business are until 7.00 p.m. or quarter to 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My mistake, Mr. Rodic. You have quarter of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell me, now, linked to the last paragraph, the following: Complaints -- a complaint lodged to the head of the EC Mission, Mr. Lucas, who in handwriting it is stated was the ambassador for human rights. So what did he state with respect to a JNA soldier captured in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lucas gave a comment. He said that while a delegation of the EC was in Dubrovnik, a dog was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did he say that when a representative of the JNA told him that he had received information that during the delegation's stay, the EC's stay, that one of their members was killed in prison?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here. I didn't attend those negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But are you familiar with this case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it. There were comments. There was -- there were comments about it, so that's how I came to hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And how do you assess this comment by Mr. Lucas with respect to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very insulting. It's impossible to make a comment on something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't need this document any more, so would the usher distribute the next document for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would you take a look at this document, please, Mr. Jokic, and tell me whether this is your own report or, rather, your response sent to Admiral Brovet, addressed to Admiral Brovet with respect to his request of the 3rd of November that we saw a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's right, that is the response.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Except for Admiral Brovet, you sent this report to the command of the 2nd Operational Group, to their attention so that they should be kept abreast and informed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Under point 1 of your report, you are informing them about the 2nd of November, from 1300 to 1420 hours, that on the positions of the 2nd Motorised Brigade in the region of Pobrezje and the 1st Motorised Brigade in the region of Golubov Kamen, that the enemy fired with a machine-gun and sniper from the positions of Babin Kuk, Mala Petka elevation 145, and Lapad elevation 36, and the Nuncijat fortress; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: For that same day, you go on to inform them about their operations from 1550 to 1620 hours on positions of the 2nd Motorised Battalion where the enemy fired a 120 mortar from the positions of Lapad, elevation 36, and 85-millimetre cannons or 40-millimetre cannons from the position of Mala Petka, elevation 145, and from the Nuncijat fortress with MB 82-millimetres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You also say that the combat deployment of the 2nd Motorised Brigade, a group was infiltrated of the ZNG and that after combat, five ZNG members were killed and one of your men, it would appear, was wounded. We can't see the exact number, but that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In your report, you also state when the units of the 472nd Motorised Brigade opened fire; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, between 1730 and 1810 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 on the second page of the document, you also mention to Admiral Brovet that a strict cease-fire had been ordered in respect of all units because the Komolac transformer station was being worked on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph on page 2, you also say: "At the same time, we guarantee that our units at the front end were not the first ones to open fire, thus there is a possibility of an improvisation of fire on the part of the MUP and ZNG on their own hotels so as to make the representatives of the EC believe that it is in fact the JNA which is breaking the cease-fire." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And in support of this assertion, you also refer to enemy operations taking place on the 3rd of November, 1991, namely that the enemy had on numerous occasions manifested activity from the region of Mokosica, Nuncijat, Srdj, and Bosanka?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And that JNA forces responded with equal fire.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what happened most often.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You also report about enemy activity on the 9th -- INTERPRETER: Interpreter's correction: 4th of November.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- of November, 1991, from the positions of Mala Petka, Babin Kuk, Nuncijat at around 1000 to 1315 hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It is stated there that the enemy opened fire with 120-millimetre mortars and probably from an 85-millimetre cannon against the positions of the 2nd Motorised Battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And, "From the fortress in the Old Town mortar fire was opened from 120-millimetre mortars on the positions of Dubac, Cibaca, Barbarela, and Brgat. One of our soldiers was wounded in the back." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you say here "from the fortress in the Old Town," is that a reference to the Old Town, the protected part of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were suspicions that from those forts of Bokari, St. John, outside the ramparts there were one or two mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In spite of the opening of enemy fire from the Old Town of Dubrovnik, in the next paragraph do you not say that the JNA did not target the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you say further on that on the 4th of November, a patrol boat was targeted by a gun of 85-millimetres from the position of Mala Petka and from a 10-millimetre cannon from Cape Brsine, that is the island of Kolocep.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At the end of this document, do you reiterate yet again what the enemy is doing, that they abuse large hotels which they describe as refugee shelters, and that is where they stationed members of the MUP and ZNG, and next to these hotels weaponry, cannons are deployed for opening fire?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is that the kind of information that you received?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You inform Admiral Brovet that the Croatia hotel in Cavtat was full of refugees while the Crisis Staff was operating in the basement of that hotel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You inform Admiral Brovet that next to the hotel a 76-millimetre cannon was captured and that from the Astarca Hotel in Srebrno, your armoured unit was held back for four hours. Was it held back by firing coming from the other side?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were operations during which a tank was set on fire at Zvekovica, in front of that hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In the report, do you assert that the hotels of Kupari, Goricina, and Pelegrin were strongholds of the members of the MUP and the ZNG and that now the strongholds are the hotels at Babin Kuk, Lazaret, and Lapad?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you emphasise to Admiral Brovet that you asked on several occasions that members of the European Community come to your front end, that is to say of your units, and to personally see for themselves who is breaching the cease-fire that had been ordered, and that the Monitoring Mission had refused to do that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was discussed, and they had accepted to come, namely that a few of them would come to see us as well. A representative came, I think he was an Italian, but later on this was given up on altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, on the basis of such a report, including your own, was this -- so this report of yours was sent to the commander of the 2nd OG, and then did the 2nd OG command write a report to Admiral Brovet and send it on the 4th of November?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask that this document be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D51.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I managed to fit into regular working hours, then this would be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well done, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of April, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
